title: model loading failure breadcrumbs - checkpoint sharding / weights download
content:
Objective: capture quick breadcrumbs from today's failed model load (reason: weights download / shard mismatch) so I don't forget and so eng can reproduce.

Summary: attempted to load 30B model with checkpoint sharded into 8 files on dedicated infra. Intermittent failures: sometimes loads fine locally, fails when pulling weights from S3 during startup on dedicated nodes. Suspect either partial object in S3 (upload incomplete), range GETs broken by proxy, or checkpoint meta mismatch (num_shards mismatch / wrong dtype).

Environment:
- infra: dedicated-gpu-prod-3 (p4d cluster, nginx proxy + internal object-proxy)
- model path: s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/
- runtime: redwood-serving v2.8.1 (commit 3f9b7d)
- loader: internal loader using smart-shard-resolver + concurrent-range-downloads
- python: 3.11, torch 2.2.0, safetensors 0.3.1

Commands / steps tried (chronological):
1) reproduce locally (works):
   git checkout 3f9b7d
   python -m runtime.loader --checkpoint s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/ --num-shards 8 --device cuda:0
   -> Model loads end-to-end locally (single machine). No errors.

2) attempt on dedicated node (fails during first shard download):
   ssh ded-gpu-03
   docker run --rm -v /etc/creds:/creds redwood/runtime:2.8.1 /bin/bash -c "python -m runtime.loader --checkpoint s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/ --num-shards 8 --device cuda:0"
   -> Failure log snippet: "\"safely open shard: shard_3.safetensors -> failed to validate length\""

3) collected stderr (excerpt):
   Traceback (most recent call last):
     File "/opt/runtime/loader.py", line 412, in load_shard
       data = download_range(url, start, end)
     File "/opt/runtime/io.py", line 78, in download_range
       resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True, timeout=30)
     File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/requests/api.py", line 76, in get
       return request('get', url, params=params, **kwargs)
   requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: ("Connection broken: IncompleteRead(512, expected 1024 bytes)", IncompleteRead(512, 512))

4) hypothesis: partial object / network proxy terminating range downloads early.
   - confirmed with curl partial GETs: curl -r 0-1023 -v https://object-proxy.internal/redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/shard_3.safetensors
   - sometimes returns 200 (full file) even when range requested -> proxy rewriting headers?

5) suspicion: object-proxy (nginx) has "proxy_buffering" or chunked encoding issues when range requests + TLS streaming combo. Also we have a custom middleware that strips Content-Range in some paths.

6) attempted workaround: reconfigure loader to do full-file GET if range fails 2x (fall back).
   - patch: runtime/io.py add fallback path after 2 range failures -> download full file into /tmp and verify checksum.
   - result: node was able to load once using fallback, but then failed on a different shard (shard_6) with checksum mismatch.

7) downloaded all shards manually from S3 (using aws cli) onto dedicated node and validated sizes/checksums:
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/shard_3.safetensors ./shard_3.safetensors
   sha256sum shard_3.safetensors  -> 7a2c... (matches expected from manifest.json)
   -> all shards appear to match manifest when pulled via aws cli. Suggests object-proxy behavior is culprit.

8) checked checkpoint metadata (manifest.json) inside checkpoint dir: fields:
   - num_shards: 8
   - dtype: float16
   - shard_map: [list of shard filenames + byte ranges]
   - expected_sizes: [..]
   -> loader uses manifest to request ranges. If proxy ignores range header, client ends up downloading entire object but code expects slice, leading to validation errors.

9) additional error noticed in logs on failing node: "safetensors.util.ValidationError: tensor data size mismatch: expected 12345678, got 2345678" -> indicates truncated read.

10) actions taken / TODO:
   - short-term: revert loader to using full-file GET by default on dedicated (config flag) until proxy fix rolled out. Add exponential backoff and verify checksums. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284)
   - medium-term: add integration test in CI that simulates object-proxy (nginx) behavior: rewrite headers / chunked responses + verify loader handles range/no-range correctly.
   - ops: open ticket with infra to inspect object-proxy logs around spikes on 2024-02-13 15:00-16:00 UTC (ded-gpu-03 reports multiple incomplete reads). Linear: RED-432 (linked).
   - long-term: switch to signed presigned URLs + direct S3 range reads for Dedicated nodes (bypass object-proxy) or implement server-side multipart+range compatibility layer.

11) other hypotheses to rule out:
   - corrupted upload: ruled out because aws cli checksums match manifest when downloaded directly from S3.
   - wrong shard_map / manifest mismatched to files: double-checked manifest.json vs objects in S3; OK.
   - differing HTTP client behavior across Python versions: improbable but note that production nodes run requests 2.31.0; locally I had 2.28.0.

Repro commands to share with infra / SRE:
- curl -I https://object-proxy.internal/redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/shard_3.safetensors
- curl -v -r 0-1023 https://object-proxy.internal/redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/shard_3.safetensors 2>&1 | tee curl_shard3.log
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/shard_3.safetensors ./ && sha256sum shard_3.safetensors
- run loader with fallback and verbose debug: RUNTIME_DEBUG=io,range python -m runtime.loader --checkpoint s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/ --num-shards 8 --device cuda:0

Notes / misc:
- I left debug prints in runtime/io.py (range headers + response.status_code + Content-Range/Content-Length) in the branch. Can share logs if needed.
- Cross-referenced with PR #1284 where fallback logic was introduced; may need to harden to verify checksum after fallback download.
- Reached out on #infra-object-store Slack with snippet; infra asked for request ids from proxy logs.

Immediate next steps for me:
- Roll PR with config flag defaulting to full GET for Dedicated only.
- Add extra verification after every shard download (compare to manifest expected size) and retry up to 3 times before failing the load.
- Pair with SRE to inspect proxy logs for the failed time window (collect request IDs) and confirm whether any middleware rewrote/stripped range requests.

If you pick this up: start with the curl reproducible steps above and attach curl_shard3.log to the ticket. If you need the manifest / expected checksums, see: s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/2024-02-13/checkpoint-8shard/manifest.json

-- Maya
